governing_table.code: No statewide building or plumbing code for private buildings. Each city or county adopts its own. Model code used here: International Building Code, the edition the state's architect and engineer licensing board uses "in the absence of any local building code"
governing_table.edition: 2018 (model text, no state amendments exist; each city's edition and amendments differ)
governing_table.table: IBC Table 2902.1 (same as International Plumbing Code Table 403.1)
governing_table.quote: Plumbing fixtures shall be provided in the minimum number as shown in Table 2902.1 based on the actual use of the building or space.
governing_table.no_statewide_code_quote: Although most relevant building codes are adopted locally, the state adopts codes for state owned buildings.
governing_table.default_edition_quote: For building design, the board shall use, in the absence of any local building code, the 2018 edition of the International Building Code, as the evaluation criteria in determining the appropriate conduct for any professional licensed or regulated by this chapter
governing_table.note: UpCodes labels this copy 'Missouri Building Code 2018, adopts without amendments IBC 2018'. That is UpCodes' label for the model code; Missouri has not adopted a statewide code. The 2026 bills to create one (SB 1431, HB 3466) did not pass: HB 3466's last House action was referral to committee on 2026-04-13.

sex_split.text: Total occupant load is divided in half, unless approved statistical data show a different split.
sex_split.quote: To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. [...] Exception: The total occupant load shall not be required to be divided in half where approved statistical data indicate a distribution of the sexes of other than 50 percent of each sex.

rounding.text: Fractions round up to the next whole number, for each sex.
rounding.quote: Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 2902.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number. For calculations involving multiple occupancies, such fractional numbers for each occupancy shall first be summed and then rounded up to the next whole number.

urinal_substitution.text: Urinals are optional. In each toilet room they may replace up to 67% of the required toilets in assembly (restaurant) and educational uses and up to 50% in all other uses, including offices. Each urinal needs a partition or screen.
urinal_substitution.quote: 424.2 Substitution for Water Closets In each bathroom or toilet room, urinals shall not be substituted for more than 67 percent of the required water closets in assembly and educational occupancies. Urinals shall not be substituted for more than 50 percent of the required water closets in all other occupancies.
urinal_substitution.note: Model 2018 International Plumbing Code text, read on UpCodes' copy filed under Kansas (UpCodes has no Missouri IPC viewer).

small_occupancy_exception.text: Separate men's and women's rooms are not required where the total occupant load is 15 or fewer, in a business occupancy of 25 or fewer, or in a store of 100 or fewer.
small_occupancy_exception.quote: Separate facilities shall not be required in structures or tenant spaces with a total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 15 or fewer. Separate facilities shall not be required in mercantile occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 100 or fewer. Separate facilities shall not be required in business occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 25 or fewer.

occupant_load.text: Office (business areas): 150 sq ft gross per occupant. Restaurant dining room (assembly without fixed seats, unconcentrated, tables and chairs): 15 sq ft net. Classroom: 20 sq ft net.
occupant_load.quote: Unconcentrated (tables and chairs) 15 net [...] Business areas 150 gross [...] Educational Classroom area 20 net

privacy.text: Every toilet used by the public or employees needs its own compartment with a door; every urinal needs side partitions.
privacy.quote: Each water closet utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate compartment with walls or partitions and a door enclosing the fixtures to ensure privacy. [...] Each urinal utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate area with walls or partitions to provide privacy.

fixtures.confidence_note: Missouri has no statewide code, so these counts are the model 2018 IBC/IPC, read on UpCodes (secondary copy; codes.iccsafe.org serves no text to a plain fetch). The city agent must replace them with each city's adopted edition and amendments.

hdpe_fire.section: No state rule (no statewide building code). Model IBC 2018 Section 803.9, which applies where a city has adopted the 2018 IBC unamended
hdpe_fire.quote: 803.9 High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) and Polypropylene (PP) Where high-density polyethylene or polypropylene is used as an interior finish, it shall comply with Section 803.1.1. | 803.1.1 Interior Wall and Ceiling Finish Materials Tested in Accordance With NFPA 286 Interior wall and ceiling finish materials shall be classified in accordance with NFPA 286 and comply with Section 803.1.1.1.
hdpe_fire.note: Whether the rule applies depends on the edition each city adopted (the HDPE section entered the IBC before 2018 and is in the 2018 model text at 803.9). City agent to confirm per city.

access.state_standard: No state accessibility code for private buildings: the federal 2010 ADA Standards apply, plus ICC A117.1 through whichever building code the city adopted (IBC 2018 references ICC A117.1-2009). For buildings built, renovated, bought or leased with state or local public funds, RSMo 8.610 to 8.655 apply: new construction and state renovations must meet 'the specifications most recently published by the American National Standards Institute' (A117.1; latest edition is 2017, not read).

differences.point: Vertical grab bar at the toilet (applies through A117.1, i.e. where the city's building code or RSMo 8.622 applies)
differences.state: ICC A117.1-2009 604.5.1: a vertical grab bar 18 inches minimum, in addition to the 42-inch side-wall bar.
differences.federal: 2010 ADA 604.5.1: "The side wall grab bar shall be 42 inches (1065 mm) long minimum, located 12 inches (305 mm) maximum from the rear wall and extending 54 inches (1370 mm) minimum from the rear wall." No vertical bar.
differences.quote: In addition, a vertical grab bar 18 inches (455 mm) minimum in length shall be mounted with the bottom of the bar located 39 inches (990 mm) minimum and 41 inches (1040 mm) maximum above the floor, and with the center line of the bar located 39 inches (990 mm) minimum and 41 inches (1040 mm) maximum from the rear wall.

differences.state: ICC A117.1-2009 604.10.2: 60 inches minimum depth and 36 inches in width.
differences.federal: 2010 ADA 604.8.2.1: "Ambulatory accessible compartments shall have a depth of 60 inches (1525 mm) minimum and a width of 35 inches (890 mm) minimum and 37 inches (940 mm) maximum."
differences.quote: The minimum area of an ambulatory accessible compartment shall be 60 inches (1525 mm) minimum in depth and 36 inches (915 mm) in width.

differences.point: Wheelchair stall door position (A117.1 gives a second option, so it is looser, not stricter; a stall must still meet the federal rule)
differences.state: ICC A117.1-2009 Table 604.9.3.1: front-partition door opening 56 inches minimum from the side wall closest to the toilet, or 4 inches maximum from the side wall farthest from it.
differences.federal: 2010 ADA 604.8.1.2: "Where located in the front partition, the door opening shall be 4 inches (100 mm) maximum from the side wall or partition farthest from the water closet."
differences.quote: Front Wall or Partition From the side wall or partition closest to the water closet 56 inches (1420 mm) minimum or From the side wall or partition farthest from the water closet 4 inches (100 mm) maximum

differences.point: Number of accessible stalls (through the model building code)
differences.state: IBC 2018 1109.2.2: at least 5 percent of compartments wheelchair accessible; where toilets plus urinals in a room total six or more, at least 5 percent ambulatory accessible in addition.
differences.federal: 2010 ADA 213.3.1: "at least one toilet compartment shall comply with 604.8.1. In addition [...] at least one compartment shall comply with 604.8.2 where six or more toilet compartments are provided, or where the combination of urinals and water closets totals six or more fixtures."
differences.quote: Where water closet compartments are provided in a toilet room or bathing room, at least 5 percent of the total number of compartments shall be wheelchair accessible. Where the combined total water closet compartments and urinals provided in a toilet room or bathing room is six or more, at least 5 percent of the total number of compartments shall be ambulatory accessible, provided in addition to the wheelchair-accessible compartment.

differences.point: Wheelchair symbol at the main entrance of publicly funded buildings
differences.federal: 2010 ADA 216: signs are required at accessible toilet rooms and entrances only where not all are accessible (216.8 read; 216.6 not quoted).
differences.quote: All buildings and facilities which are constructed pursuant to the standards, principles and specifications set forth in sections 8.610 to 8.650, and any other building or facility which provides access for physically disabled persons shall prominently display at the main entrance to the building or facility the international wheelchair accessibility symbol.

public_buildings_statute.scope_quote: The principles, standards and specifications set forth in sections 8.610 to 8.650 shall apply to all public parks, recreation areas, rest areas, parking spaces, parking lots, curbs, sidewalks, public accommodations, buildings and facilities for public use and assembly that are constructed, renovated, purchased or leased in whole or in part with the use of state funds or the funds of any political subdivision of this state.
public_buildings_statute.standard_quote: In all renovation and new construction undertaken by this state, and in all new construction undertaken by any political subdivision of this state, the standard specifications for making such public improvements accessible to and usable by the physically disabled shall be the specifications most recently published by the American National Standards Institute, Inc. (ANSI).
public_buildings_statute.renovation_quote: Public toilets shall be arranged to allow traffic and use of persons in wheelchairs and shall provide at least one toilet stall which is a minimum of thirty-six inches wide and fifty-six inches long, has a door, if doors are used, that is thirty-two inches wide and swings out, and has handrails on each side which are thirty-three inches above the floor.
public_buildings_statute.renovation_note: RSMo 8.620 lets a city or county choose, for its own renovations, between the ANSI standard and this older statutory list. It is weaker than the federal standard, which still applies.

access.process: No state plan review or registration for accessibility was found. Enforcement of RSMo 8.610 to 8.650 on publicly funded buildings sits with the Department of Elementary and Secondary Education (state school funds), the state agency in charge of design (state funds) or the local governing body (local funds), per RSMo 8.630; deviations need the Commissioner of Administration's permission after consulting the Governor's Council on Disability (RSMo 8.650). On private buildings, the city's building department reviews accessibility with the building permit.

single_user.rule: No Missouri statute or state code on single-user restroom signs. It depends on the city's adopted code: the model 2018 code says single-user rooms 'shall be identified for use by either sex'; the model 2021 code says 'available for use by all persons regardless of their sex'.
single_user.quote: 2018: "Single-user toilet facilities and bathing rooms, and family or assisted-use toilet rooms and bathing rooms shall be identified for use by either sex." | 2021: "Single-user toilet and bathing rooms, and family or assisted-use toilet rooms and bathing rooms shall be identified as being available for use by all persons regardless of their sex."

all_gender_shared.rule: No state rule. Under the model 2018 code, separate facilities for each sex are required above the small-occupancy limits, with no exception for a shared multi-stall room. The model 2021 code adds an exception allowing rooms designed for both sexes where toilets have privacy compartments and urinals are in stalls or visually separated. Which applies depends on the city's edition.
all_gender_shared.quote: 2021 IBC 2902.2 exception 6: "Separate facilities shall not be required where rooms having both water closets and lavatory fixtures are designed for use by both sexes and privacy for water closets are installed in accordance with Section 405.3.4 of the International Plumbing Code. Urinals shall be located in an area visually separated from the remainder of the facility or each urinal that is provided shall be located in a stall." 2018 IBC 2902.2: "Where plumbing fixtures are required, separate facilities shall be provided for each sex."

use_restrictions.rule: None in force found. HCS HB 2536 (2026), which would have required multi-occupancy restrooms in public buildings, public schools, state colleges and correctional facilities to be designated for one sex, passed the House 101 to 48 on 2026-04-20 and was voted do pass by a Senate committee on 2026-05-05; the House's action list shows no later action, so it did not become law in the 2026 session.
use_restrictions.quote: 4/20/2026 H 1855 - 1856 Third Read and Passed (H) - AYES: 101 NOES: 48 PRESENT: 0 [...] 5/05/2026 Executive Session Held (S) 5/05/2026 Voted Do Pass (S)

public_wage.law: Missouri Prevailing Wage Law, RSMo 290.210 to 290.340
public_wage.threshold: Does not apply where the engineer's estimate or accepted bid for the total project cost is $75,000 or less. Maintenance work (repair without replacement) is excluded.
public_wage.who_sets: Missouri Department of Labor and Industrial Relations, Division of Labor Standards: an Annual Wage Order by July 1 each year, by county and occupational title. Where fewer than 1,000 hours were reported for a title in a county, the 'public works contracting minimum wage' (120% of the county's average hourly wage) applies instead.
public_wage.quote: The provisions of sections 290.210 to 290.340 shall not apply to the construction of public works for which either the engineer's estimate or the bid accepted by the public body for the total project cost is in the amount of seventy-five thousand dollars or less. | Division page: "Missouri's Prevailing Wage Law establishes a minimum wage rate for public works projects in Missouri valued over $75,000. [...] The prevailing wage rate differs by county and for different types of work. Every year, the Division of Labor Standards will release a final Annual Wage Order by July 1."

sales_tax.state_rate_quote: The 4.225 percent state sales and use tax is distributed into four funds [...] Cities and counties may impose a local sales and use tax.

shipped_goods.rule: Taxable. A seller outside Missouri must collect the tax once its taxable sales delivered into Missouri exceed $100,000 in the previous or current calendar year. If the seller does not collect it, the buyer must file a use tax return and pay (no return needed if untaxed out-of-state purchases total under $2,000 in the year). Local use tax applies only where the city or county has adopted one.
shipped_goods.quote: RSMo 144.605(2)(e): "Selling tangible personal property for delivery into this state, provided the seller's gross receipts from taxable sales from delivery of tangible personal property into this state in the previous calendar year or current calendar year exceeds one hundred thousand dollars." | 12 CSR 10-103.250(2)(A): "Generally, if a taxpayer does not pay use tax to a seller on out-of-state purchases of tangible personal property for use, storage or consumption in this state, the taxpayer must file a use tax return and remit the tax."

freight.rule: Usual and customary delivery charges that are stated separately are not taxed (sales tax and use tax). Freight folded into the price is taxed. Note: the Department's rule 12 CSR 10-103.600(3)(A) still says a separately stated shipping charge is taxed when the buyer is required to pay it; the statute's wording is later and broader. Confirm with the Department.
freight.quote: RSMo 144.605(8): "The sales price shall not include usual and customary delivery charges that are separately stated." | RSMo 144.010: "The term gross receipts shall not include usual and customary delivery charges that are stated separately from the sale price"

install_labor.rule: Not taxed. Missouri taxes services only where a statute names them, and installation or construction labor is not on the Department's list of taxable services. For goods bought from out of state, the use tax 'sales price' excludes labor charged for installing the property. Where a seller sells and installs, a separately stated service charge is not taxed.
install_labor.quote: RSMo 144.605(8): "'sales price' shall not include [...] the amount charged for labor or services rendered in installing or applying the property sold" | 12 CSR 10-103.600(1): "The sale of a service is not subject to tax unless a specific statute authorizes the taxation of the service."

furnish_and_install.rule: The contractor is the final consumer of materials that become part of the real property: the contractor pays sales or use tax when buying the partitions and does not charge tax on the contract, provided title passes after installation (the default). If title passes to the customer before attachment, the contractor instead collects tax on the item's sale price. Contractors on jobs for exempt entities (public and private schools, political subdivisions, churches, charities) can buy materials tax free with the entity's project exemption certificate.
furnish_and_install.quote: 12 CSR 10-112.010(1): "In general, a contractor is the final user and consumer of the materials and supplies used and consumed in fulfilling a construction contract and which become part of a completed real property improvement." (3)(A): "If title passes after the attachment, the contractor is subject to tax on its purchase of the tangible personal property and does not collect tax on its transfer of ownership or title of the item. In general, title passes after installation is complete, unless the contractor and purchaser expressly agree otherwise."

page.stalls_intro: Missouri has no statewide building code, so each city sets its own toilet counts. The model rules Missouri cities build on count toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area, with half counted as men and half as women. Every toilet needs a stall. Urinals are optional: in a men's room they may replace up to half of the toilets in an office and up to two thirds in a restaurant or school, and each urinal needs a screen.
page.stalls_after: These figures come from the model rules, before any city changes. They are minimums for the whole building, and at least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.
page.capacity: The model rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** Missouri has no statewide building code, so this rule comes from your city's code. The model rules Missouri cities build on require solid plastic (HDPE) partitions to pass a room fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.access_bullet: - **Wheelchair access:** a restroom with stalls needs at least one stall a wheelchair user can enter and use. Federal law sets the sizes, and the city's building code adds a national accessibility standard on top. Missouri has no state review of plans for access: the city checks it with the building permit.
page.state_extra_bullet: - **Missouri extras:** the national standard that Missouri cities apply through their building codes asks for an 18 inch vertical grab bar on the side wall next to the toilet, which the federal rules do not. On buildings paid for with state, city, county or school district money, Missouri law requires the latest edition of that standard and the wheelchair symbol at the main entrance.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** Missouri has no state law on single-user or all-gender restrooms, and none on who may use which restroom. The city's building code decides how a one-person restroom is signed and whether a shared all-gender room is allowed.
page.public_jobs: On state, city, county and school district projects with a total cost above $75,000, Missouri law requires at least the wage the state sets each year for each trade in each county.
page.tax_install_bullet: - **Tax on installation:** in Missouri, installation labor is not taxed. A contractor who supplies and installs partitions pays the tax when buying them and does not add tax to the contract.
page.tax_ship_bullet: - **Buying without installation:** partitions shipped to {city} are taxable. Usual delivery charges listed separately on the invoice are not taxed. If the seller doesn't collect the tax, the buyer owes it to the state.
page.tax_confirm: your accountant or the Missouri Department of Revenue
sources: - Missouri has no statewide building or plumbing code for private buildings: [International Code Council, Missouri adoptions](https://www.iccsafe.org/advocacy/adoptions-map/missouri/) ("most relevant building codes are adopted locally"); the state's licensing board for architects and engineers uses the 2018 International Building Code "in the absence of any local building code": [20 CSR 2030-2.040](https://www.sos.mo.gov/cmsimages/adrules/csr/current/20csr/20c2030-2.pdf). The 2026 bill to create a statewide code did not pass: [HB 3466 actions](https://house.mo.gov/BillActions.aspx?bill=HB3466&year=2026&code=R). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Toilet counts under the model rules: 2018 International Building Code, [Table 2902.1 and Sections 2902.1.1 and 2902.2](https://up.codes/viewer/missouri/ibc-2018/chapter/29/plumbing-systems), [Table 1004.5 (floor area per person)](https://up.codes/viewer/missouri/ibc-2018/chapter/10/means-of-egress) and [Section 1209.3 (stalls and urinal screens)](https://up.codes/viewer/missouri/ibc-2018/chapter/12/interior-environment), and 2018 International Plumbing Code, [Section 424.2 (urinals)](https://up.codes/viewer/kansas/ipc-2018/chapter/4/fixtures-faucets-and-fixture-fittings), all read on UpCodes, a secondary copy. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Fire test for solid plastic partitions under the model rules: 2018 International Building Code, [Sections 803.9 and 803.1.1 (NFPA 286)](https://up.codes/viewer/missouri/ibc-2018/chapter/8/interior-finishes), read on UpCodes. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Stall rules compared: [ICC A117.1-2009, Section 604](https://up.codes/viewer/missouri/icc-a117.1-2009/chapter/6/plumbing-elements-and-facilities) (read on UpCodes), referenced by the [2018 International Building Code, Section 1109.2](https://up.codes/viewer/missouri/ibc-2018/chapter/11/accessibility), against the [2010 ADA Standards](https://www.access-board.gov/ada/), sections 213 and 604. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Access rules for publicly funded buildings: Revised Statutes of Missouri, sections [8.610](https://revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=8.610), [8.620](https://revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=8.620), [8.622](https://revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=8.622), [8.630](https://revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=8.630), [8.650](https://revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=8.650) and [8.655](https://revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=8.655). Checked 2026-11-24.

- No Missouri restroom-use law in force: [HB 2536 (2026) actions, Missouri House](https://house.mo.gov/BillActions.aspx?bill=HB2536&year=2026&code=R) (passed the House, no final passage). Single-user and shared-room wording in the model rules: International Building Code Section 2902, [2018](https://up.codes/viewer/missouri/ibc-2018/chapter/29/plumbing-systems) and [2021](https://up.codes/viewer/missouri/ibc-2021/chapter/29/plumbing-systems) editions, read on UpCodes. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Wages on public jobs: Missouri Prevailing Wage Law, Revised Statutes of Missouri sections [290.210](https://revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=290.210), [290.230](https://revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=290.230) and [290.257](https://revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=290.257); [Missouri Division of Labor Standards, Prevailing Wage](https://labor.mo.gov/dls/prevailing-wage) (annual wage orders). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Sales tax: [Missouri Department of Revenue, Sales/Use Tax](https://dor.mo.gov/taxation/business/tax-types/sales-use/) (4.225% state rate); Revised Statutes of Missouri sections [144.010](https://revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=144.010) and [144.605](https://revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=144.605) (delivery charges, installation labor, out-of-state sellers); [12 CSR 10-112.010, Contractors](https://www.sos.mo.gov/cmsimages/adrules/csr/current/12csr/12c10-112.pdf); [12 CSR 10-103.250 and 10-103.600](https://www.sos.mo.gov/cmsimages/adrules/csr/current/12csr/12c10-103.pdf); [Department of Revenue, Taxable Services](https://dor.mo.gov/faq/taxation/business/taxable-services.html). Checked 2026-11-24.
page.official_names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design; ICC A117.1 as referenced by the city's building code (2009 edition under the 2018 International Building Code), and the most recent ANSI A117.1 for publicly funded buildings under RSMo 8.610 to 8.655; no statewide building or plumbing code (each city adopts an edition of the International Building Code and its own plumbing code); NFPA 286 for HDPE.

City agent to replace.
codes.iccsafe.org returned no code text to a plain fetch; model code quotes come from UpCodes (secondary). UpCodes' 'Missouri Building Code 2018' label is its own; no such state code exists.

ICC A117.1-2017 (the 'most recently published' ANSI standard that RSMo 8.622 requires on public construction) was not read; the vertical grab bar and other stall differences were read in the 2009 edition only. Confirm with the Governor's Council on Disability or the project architect.

Whether SB 1431 (statewide building code) had any Senate action after February 2026: the Senate bill page did not open. HB 3466, its House twin, stopped in committee (official House page). Recheck in the 2027 session.
HB 2536 (restrooms by sex in public buildings and schools) did not pass in 2026 per the House action list; a similar bill may return in 2027. Recheck before launch.

Freight: RSMo 144.010 and 144.605 exclude separately stated 'usual and customary delivery charges', while 12 CSR 10-103.600(3)(A) still taxes a mandatory shipping charge. Confirm with the Missouri Department of Revenue (or Abe's accountant) how freight on partitions shipped from out of state is treated.
